From what I can see, the camera forward points toward -Z direction in local space. Therefore, we would expect that this method will rotate the camera to "look" at `target` correctly. However, if we use `look_at` for other cases, we will assume that it points the +Z direction toward `target` instead. Also, the method's document mentions the `local z direction`, not +Z or -Z direction. This is kinda confusing.

body:
> However, if we use `look_at` for other cases, we will assume that it points the +Z direction toward `target` instead.

Why?

I was discussing this on Discord a couple of weeks ago when someone asked "what is forward?" Initially I was going to say that it is just -Z, but the answer became more complicated as I thought about it. It is kind of an implicit direction defined by the entity being transformed. For example, if you load a humanoid model where it looks along +Z in right-handed y-up, and give it an identity transform, then its 'forward' is along +Z. If it were looking along +X then forward for it would be along +X.

However, for a camera, because we use right-handed y-up perspective projections, that means that forward is explicitly along -Z. Maybe it is standard to consider forward as being out of the screen because that is how assets are modelled?

What is the expectation for the forward-facing direction of a model that is imported into a right-handed y-up application? I feel like it should face along the -Z axis and that this Transform::look_at implementation is wrong for a right-handed y-up world. But perhaps that is not the broader convention?

I asked @aclysma for input on this as I figured they may have insight. They provided [this link to where glTF explicitly defines the coordinate space of the models as right-handed y-up **_with forward along +z_**!](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/master/specification/2.0#coordinate-system-and-units) So that's one reference point. Do other model formats define what is forward as well? That would be great if so! :) Though it may mean that you need to convert from that format's definition of forward to whatever you want to use as your internal engine idea of forward at import-time. But as you may need to convert between coordinate spaces anyway, I guess that isn't a big problem.

I have to agree with @Looooong's comment that the documentation's confusing. Bevy seems to use [WebGPU's](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#coordinate-systems) right-handed y-up coordinate system which will mean a choice between -Z as fwd, +X as right vs +Z fwd, -X right with the former being in use as evidenced by the current `look_at` implementation and the `forward` method on the Transform types. glTF uses the [-X is right](https://www.khronos.org/registry/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#coordinate-system-and-units) convention but I think that'd be even more confusing for a game application. -Z fwd is at least familiar for people coming from Godot.

That being said, there's no bug in the `look_at` code as per the conventions bevy seems to be following now.

issue.body:
## Bevy version

`0.8.0`

## What you did

1. Spawn entity from glTF scene with recognizable forward direction (e.g. character, vehicle).
2. Transform the entity along the Transform::forward() direction.
3. Observe model moving backward.

## What you expected

Model moves forward.

## What went wrong
Both Bevy and glTF use a right-handed Y-up coordinate system. They do however disagree on what direction is forward and right:

- glTF defines forward as +Z and right as -X (see [https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.pdf](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#coordinate-system-and-units)).
- Bevy's Transform defines forward as -Z and right as +X (see https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/prelude/struct.Transform.html#method.right and https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/prelude/struct.Transform.html#method.forward).

## Possible solutions

1. glTF importer negates X and Z coordinates during import (breaking change for all bevy apps that use glTF import).
2. Bevy Transform is changed to follow the glTF convention (breaking change for all bevy apps that use one of the Transform's direction functions).
3. Bevy stops defining a forward, back, left, right direction and leaves it up to the user (e.g. by changing the forward, back, left, right functions on Transform to local_neg_z, local_z, local_x, local_neg_x).

In any case, Bevy should be consistent regarding its coordinate system. Currently, the look_at function follows the glTF convention and not the Transform's definition of forward and right (see https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/1153)
